harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented a password complexity policy on node1 (pam_pwquality minlen=12, minclass=3) using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node with ansible installed). Functionally verified weak-password rejection and compliant-password acceptance, then executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2, confirming changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Identified node2 as the control node (has ansible/ansible-playbook; node1 does not)
Repaired node1 sshd (regenerated missing host keys via ssh-keygen -A, cleared systemd restart-rate-limit with systemctl reset-failed, started ssh.service) so Ansible could reach it
Wired passwordless SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster keypair; fixed known_hosts and ansible.cfg IdentityFile override via ansible_ssh_private_key_file in inventory

Wrote /root/ansible/inventory.ini and /root/ansible/password-complexity.yml on node2: installs libpam-pwquality, sets minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, and inserts 'password requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3' before the pam_unix.so line in /etc/pam.d/common-password
Ran the playbook against node1 (ok=5, changed=4) and verified resulting pwquality.conf and PAM stack content

Functionally tested on a disposable test user: a self-service passwd change rejected a short/low-complexity password (BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] than 12 characters) and accepted a 12+ character 3-class password (password updated successfully); confirmed root-initiated passwd only warns (expected pam_pwquality root-bypass), so enforcement was proven via the user's own passwd session; removed the test user afterward
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, pwquality.conf values, PAM line, package state, ansible/service health) on node1 and node2

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'reboot' (ack returned before disconnect), confirmed transient unreachability, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed from 242af11e... to 06f3965f..., and verified pwquality.conf, PAM line, and libpam-pwquality package all persisted post-reboot
Restarted node2 via the same pattern, confirmed transient unreachability, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed from 416c5cf5... to 0814deeb..., and verified ansible/playbook files intact
Re-ran the playbook after both restarts: ok=5, changed=0 (idempotent), confirming end-to-end recovery of both the control node and the enforced policy on node1

evidence.requirement: node1 requires minlen=12 and minclass=3 password policy, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Ansible inventory/playbook authored on control node node2 and applied to node1; verified pwquality.conf shows minlen=12/minclass=3 and pam_pwquality.so is requisite ahead of pam_unix.so in common-password

evidence.requirement: Functional proof the policy rejects weak passwords and accepts compliant ones
evidence.summary: Test user's self-service passwd change: 'short1' rejected repeatedly with BAD PASSWORD (too short) until retries exhausted; 'Str0ng!Pass99' (13 chars, 3 classes) accepted with 'password updated successfully'; test user then removed

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, ssh ActiveState, pwquality.conf/PAM values on node1 and boot_id/ansible availability on node2 prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node1 became unreachable (connection timed out) then reachable again with boot_id changed from 242af11e-... to 06f3965f-...; post-restart check confirms pwquality.conf, PAM line, and libpam-pwquality package intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node2 became unreachable then reachable again with boot_id changed from 416c5cf5-... to 0814deeb-...; subsequent idempotent playbook re-run (ok=5, changed=0) proves control-node ansible tooling and node1's enforced policy both recovered fully
